svg.title: Midnight at the Diner, diner drawing
svg.desc: Fictional AWS architecture. Store connectors sign API requests. Identity-to-store bindings, event IDs and monotonic source versions must be checked server-side; a store ID in JSON is not authority. Fargate placements in AZ A/B are alternative execution capacity, not permission to execute each stock mutation twice. Reconciliation uses transactional checkpoints and bounded retries. Journal-read paths and VPC endpoints are omitted. The supervisor callback releases a workflow approval step. Supplier ordering and payment are outside the view. Catch paths carry execution/checkpoint identifiers for recovery. The Aurora icon is an aggregate cluster, not a single-instance HA claim. Cross-account backup needs supported resources, organization configuration, copy roles, KMS permissions, retention and tested restoration. Store sync connector to Store identity API; Store identity API to Validate and deduplicate; Validate and deduplicate to Versioned stock journal; Nightly schedule to Reconcile and approve; Reconcile and approve to Reconcile tasks A; Reconcile and approve to Reconcile tasks B; Reconcile tasks A to Transactional stock DB; Reconcile tasks B to Transactional stock DB; Supervisor sign-in to Approve supplier draft; Approve supplier draft to Reconcile and approve; Reconcile and approve to Operator failure alert; Transactional stock DB to Inventory backup vault. Boundary labels distinguish accounts, regions, VPCs, AZs, subnets and logical groups. These annotations do not verify deployed isolation or permissions.

g.title: Store workload signs requests with its own IAM role; configured API resource policy limits integration accounts.
Connector includes store ID and monotonic event version; backend checks identity-to-store binding.
Conditional event-ID insertion and version checks tolerate offline replay without double counting.
Scheduler starts a bounded execution, not an unbounded retry loop.
Orchestrator starts reconciliation work with explicit retry and timeout policies.
Alternative AZ placement is capacity, not a second execution of the same stock mutation.
Transactional stock updates; a VPC endpoint permits journal reads that are omitted from the drawing.
Shared cluster enforces idempotent reconciliation checkpoints.
Verified supervisor membership authorizes a supplier-proposal approval, not unrestricted inventory writes.
Authenticated callback releases the approval step; supplier execution remains outside this view.
Catch path notifies an operator with execution ID and failed checkpoint.
Scheduled cross-account backup copy requires supported resources, backup roles and encryption permissions.
